title: CX23 Biological Microscope Instructions
locator: Page 5, optional accessories. Chapter 3, brightfield observation, p. 7. Chapter 4, operation and immersion objective, pp. 8–13.
summary: The brightfield sequence shows how to focus on a mounted slide, change objectives and set the aperture for the selected objective. The accessory list identifies the eyepiece micrometer and 100× objective.
scope: This edition shows the binocular CX23. Check the installed objectives and the availability of a calibrated scale or camera before using published measurements.

title: Harmonized methods of melissopalynology
publisher: Apidologie, via the International Honey Commission
version: von der Ohe et al., volume 35, pp. S18–S25. DOI 10.1051/apido:2004050
locator: Section 2.2 and Figure 1, counts across a prepared slide. Section 2.4 and Table I, interpretation by pollen type. Section 3, absolute counts.
summary: The harmonized method uses systematic traverses of prepared honey sediment at 400–1000× total magnification to estimate the proportion of each pollen type. A separate filtration and counting procedure estimates the absolute number of plant elements.
scope: Botanical identification requires reference slides and taxonomic experience. Different plants contribute different amounts of pollen per unit of nectar, so percentages alone can mislead when assigning a floral origin.
rights: Commission-hosted publication link and original catalog summary.

title: Melissopalynological investigations of seasonal honey samples from the Greater Kruger National Park, Savanna biome of South Africa
locator: Materials and methods, slide analysis with the Axioscope 5. Plate 1, photographed pollen types. Section 3.1 and Figure 2, relative composition.
summary: The researchers examined pollen from 38 honey samples across four seasons on a ZEISS Axioscope 5, using reference collections to identify the grains. Combretum-type pollen averaged 56% across their samples.
scope: The counts describe the South African Lowveld sites and seasons sampled. Summer observations came from one hive. Local interpretation needs an appropriate pollen reference collection and comparable sampling.

title: Identification of pollen taxa by different microscopy techniques
version: Pospiech et al., article e0256808. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0256808
locator: Materials and methods, microscope and image acquisition. Abstract and Results, classification rates for brightfield, darkfield and phase contrast.
summary: The team compared automated classification of 2,482 pollen grains from seven botanical taxa. Their brightfield images gave 88.88% correct classification and phase contrast gave 93.05%. The paper describes the imaging setup behind these rates.
scope: The study used a Nikon Eclipse Ci-L, a motorized stage and a camera. Its classifier performance applies to those images and taxa. A routine visual count or a different regional pollen collection needs its own checks.

title: Measuring Stomatal Density using nail varnish
locator: Page 1, Method steps 1–5, making an impression and choosing replicate counting fields.
summary: The method uses a transparent leaf-surface impression to count stomata in several graticule squares or microscope fields. For leaves that yield a suitable epidermal peel, the authors also describe direct viewing on a slide.
scope: Some leaves brown or fail to produce an impression. To compare densities per unit area, measure the area represented by a square or field at the chosen magnification and keep track of the leaf side.

title: Investigating Leaf Epidermal Traits and Their Impact on Fruit Yield of Watermelons
locator: Materials and methods, Microscopic examination and data collection. Table 2, stomatal dimensions and counts by leaf surface and variety.
summary: Using an Olympus CX23, the authors compared the upper and lower leaf surfaces of four watermelon varieties. Table 2 distinguishes stomatal density from stomatal index and reports each by variety and leaf side.
scope: The authors used prepared epidermal sections and a calibrated ocular micrometer for dimensions. Keep the preparation and leaf side consistent when comparing these data with varnish impressions.

title: Divergent effects of successive drought and flooding on photosynthesis in wheat and barley
locator: Section 2.4, field-area calibration and image measurements. Section 3.3 and Figure 4, stomatal counts and sizes by crop and treatment.
summary: The researchers photographed impressions of the upper leaf surface, calibrated the field area with a microscope scale and expressed counts per square millimetre. Following flooding then drought, barley had higher stomatal density, while wheat showed no significant change.
scope: The authors used a GXML 2800 setup with a camera and sampled defined leaf positions at recovery. This comparison depends on crop, leaf position and timing. Calibrate the field area for the local optical setup.
